title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 49-50
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 49 to 50 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत्'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 49 to 50 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 49 to 50.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 49 to 50** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत्**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत् । मनोहरो जितक्रोधो वीरबाहुर्विदारणः ॥** **स्वापनः स्ववशो व्यापी नैकात्मा नैककर्मकृत् । वत्सरो वत्सलो वत्सी रत्नगर्भो धनेश्वरः ॥**

Of noble vows, fair of face, subtle, with a pleasing sound is he. The giver of happiness and the true friend is that God of gods. He steals the heart, has conquered anger, has heroic arms and tears down evil. He lulls the world to rest, he is his own master, he is all-pervading. Of many forms and doing many works is that God of gods. The year, full of tenderness, holding jewels within, lord of wealth.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 49 to 50 mean?
faq.a: Of noble vows, fair of face, subtle, with a pleasing sound is he. The giver of happiness and the true friend is that God of gods. He steals the heart, has conquered anger, has heroic arms and tears down evil. He lulls the world to rest, he is his own master, he is all-pervading. Of many forms and doing many works is that God of gods. The year, full of tenderness, holding jewels within, lord of wealth.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
